# nonSafeInteger

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a safe integer.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonSafeInteger() — Checks whether a value is **not** a safe integer. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonSafeInteger<T>(value: T | number): value is T;
```

`nonSafeInteger(value)` is the same test as `!isSafeInteger(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An integer that an IEEE-754 double represents exactly. Beyond that range distinct mathematical integers collapse onto the same value and arithmetic quietly stops being exact.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| number` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a safe integer; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2); // => true
nonSafeInteger(1.5); // => true
nonSafeInteger("42"); // => true
nonSafeInteger(42); // => false
nonSafeInteger(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); // => false
```
